01.divergence: No direct Rahasya passage matching the recording’s spoken introduction was assigned.

02.divergence: No direct Rahasya passage matches these introductory verses. The timed recording caption supports the displayed Tantrasāra-saṅgraha 70 and Kṛṣṇāmṛta-mahārṇava 4, 14 and 122 lines. A short Sanskrit phrase around 03:35–03:43 remains too uncertain in the caption for a reliable reading and is not printed as verified text.

03.divergence: The recording’s practical setup emphasizes two principal kalaśas. The Rahasya’s full item list distinguishes nine water vessels by purpose; see printed pp. 253–254.
03.action: Prepare tulasi and all external materials; collect and protect water for the specified puja uses as described under Agryodaka. Set out the book’s full item list: śālagrāma, two cakrāṅkita stones, Sudarśana, the selected Viṣṇu and attendant icons, sampuṭa, somasūtra plate and tripod, nine purpose-specific water vessels, conch, two lamps, bell, containers for gandha/akṣata/aṅgāra, turmeric and kumkum, tulasī and flowers, tāmbūla, coconut, dakṣiṇā, ārati ladles and kṛṣṇājina. Prepare the specified fragrance paste and akṣata.
03.contemplate: Treat bhakti, Hari’s supremacy, taratamya, dependence on Hari, golaka contemplation, and the mantras as the inner requisites; tulasi is supreme among external requisites.

04.divergence: The recording’s early tīrtha-prāśana is not the same sequence as the Rahasya’s post-abhisheka handling of Lakshmi, Vayu, Sesha and Garuda tirthas. The Rahasya timing and recipients are stated in the linked passage.

05.divergence: No direct Rahasya passage matching the recording’s Guru–Hari–Madhva salutation at the door was located. Devagruha Pravesha is assigned to the later doorway and entry steps.

06.action: Offer namaskara to the gatekeepers; chant the Vayu mantra, clap three times, enter, then chant “Vande Vishnum” and salute the devatas and gurus.
06.contemplate: Visualize the sixteen entrances and their guardians, including the four named cardinal gate-sets.

07.action: Light the lamps while chanting “Agnina agni…”.
07.contemplate: See Srihari as present throughout the shrine and in every item used in worship.

08.action: Chant “Vande Vishnum” and offer pranams to the stated devatas and gurus.
08.contemplate: Remember Srihari’s supremacy while honoring the hierarchy.

09.divergence: The recording uses its own bhutocchatana wording and gestures. The Rahasya additionally specifies look/flowers/heel actions, Naracha mudra, Vayustuti prayers, and a seated Chotika-mudra “Apakramantu” stage.
09.action: Remove obstacles by look, flowers, heel-thumping and three claps as applicable; chant “Apasarpantu…” and use Naracha mudra for dikbandhana. At the seated stage use Chotika mudra with “Apakramantu…”.
09.contemplate: Pray to Rudra, Vayu within Rudra, and Narasimha within that Vayu to remove hindrances caused by asuras, bhutas and pishachas.

10.action: Place a darbha mat on a wooden plank, deer skin above the mat, and a clean cloth over the skin. Bow to Hari and the named supporting devatās. Show Iṣu (arrow) mudrā to bind the four directions, then raise the hands and show Cakra mudrā in every direction before sitting and proceeding to prāṇāyāma and saṅkalpa.
10.contemplate: Remember Hari as the master of Ādhāra Śakti, Maṇḍūka, Kūrma, Varāha, Śeṣa, Kālāgnirudra, Vajra and Pṛthvī beneath the seat. Envision Sudarśana protecting the worshipper in all directions.

11.action: With folded hands ask Srihari to bear the human smell; chant “Ebhyo maataa…”.
11.contemplate: His aprakrta body has sacred fragrance; human bodily impurity should not be brought near Him casually.

12.action: Imagine a thin screen before Srihari, sit on the raised platform, chant Brahmapara Stotra, then worship free of doshas.
12.contemplate: Its recitation removes grave sins and inner faults such as raga, dvesha, jealousy, ego, moha and mamata, giving fitness for puja.

13.action: Recognize and invoke Brahma, Garuda, Sesha, Saraswati and Prajapati in the bell; ring it before puja and during abhisheka, dhupa, deepa, naivedya, alankara and shayana.
13.contemplate: The bell admits devatas and divine power and drives asuras away; visualize the resident devatas in its parts.

14.action: Meditate on the mantapa, remove the face-covering with “uttapto…”, pray “krupayottiiyatam…” and “Aayatabhyaam…”, awaken Srihari and place Him in the mantapa.
14.contemplate: See the detailed golden, gem-filled temple, birds, tank, fragrances, lamps, altar, throne and prepared seat exactly as the source describes.

15.action: Place nirmalya in the vessel on the Lord’s left (worshipper’s right) for Rudra, chanting Ambhruni Sukta; remove nirmalya from Lakshmi, Vayu, Sesha and Garuda as well.
15.contemplate: Rudra waits with a vessel on his head to receive the Lord’s prior offerings.

16.action: Abhisheka the shankha first and discard that water; then abhisheka Srihari with the shankha and discard it before the nirmalya-tirtha abhisheka.
16.contemplate: Maintain the distinct destinations of each water.

17.divergence: The recording labels this water purification; the Rahasya’s matching material locates the preparatory nyasas and invocations before Suddhabhisheka.

18.action: For Lakshmi, perform abhisheka with the listed mantras; discard first water, sprinkle the second on the head, and keep the remainder separately without drinking it.

19.action: Perform the shankha abhisheka first; discard its water as directed.
19.contemplate: Keep shankha water distinct from subsequent tirtha.

20.action: Abhisheka Vayu twice, discarding the first water; chant the named Vayu texts for the second and keep its tirtha separately to drink after puja.
20.contemplate: Vayu tirtha alone is explicitly to be received.

21.action: Abhisheka Sesha and Garuda twice; discard first water and only sprinkle the second tirtha on the head. Worship only Lakshmi, Vayu, Sesha and Garuda in Srihari’s presence.
21.contemplate: Other devatas and gurus are worshipped after Srihari’s worship is completed.

22.action: Meditate on the mantapa before uncovering and awakening the pratima.
22.contemplate: Visualize the temple, threshold, birds, lotus-tank, fragrance, gem lamps, gold and crystal architecture, pearl pillars, seat and chamaras in the complete source description.

23.contemplate: Contemplate Hari’s relation to the reflected bimba as described in the source.

24.action: Do pranayama, then make sankalpa with day, tithi and nakshatra, resolving to perform puja with devotion.
24.contemplate: Hari alone makes all action possible; perform only by His strength and prompting, for His pleasure.

25.action: Place the larger Snānīya Bṛhat Kalaśa and smaller Pūrṇa Kalaśa. Use the conch for water from the first and pour directly from the second. Show Śaṅkha, Cakra, Gadā, Padma, Dhenu, Garuḍa, Candra, Nārāca and Haṃsa mudrās with their mantras. With a tulasī leaf draw a six-cornered lotus on each water surface; hold the right hand above the vessels. Add gandha, tulasī and flowers. Invoke Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa within Vāyu and the water deities Budha and Varuṇa. Touch the kalaśas and recite 'Kalaśasya mukhe Viṣṇuḥ'; recognize Viṣṇu at the mouth, Rudra at the neck, Brahmā at the base, the Mātṛ-gaṇas and hundred Aja forms in the middle, and the oceans, seven islands, Vedas and Vedāṅgas within. Invite the named goddesses, rivers, oceans and sacred waters.
25.contemplate: Visualize the kalasha as containing the complete sacred cosmos: devatas, seven oceans and islands, the world, the four Vedas and their auxiliaries. See Srihari’s special presence established through the nyasas and moola mantra.

26.action: Invite Gaṅgā, Yamunā, Sarasvatī, Śutudrī, Asiknī, Godāvarī, Narmadā, Sindhu, Kāverī and the waters' presiding deities. Recite the two river mantras and add tulasī to both kalaśas. Worship Nārāyaṇa, Vāsudeva, Pradyumna and Aniruddha around the bathing kalaśa with gandha and tulasī. Perform pīṭha worship for both vessels. Invoke Nārāyaṇa with the forms Aja through Śiṃśumāra in the bathing kalaśa and in reverse order in the Pūrṇa Kalaśa; contemplate those forms arriving from Sūrya. Perform Mātṛkā-, Tattva-, Kṛddholka and other aṅga-nyāsas, then akṣara-nyāsa. Touch both vessels, recite 'Udyad bhāsvat' and repeat the mūla mantra twelve times. Request the deities to remain through worship and accept it.
26.contemplate: See the invoked devatas, sacred waters, Vedas and kshetras truly present in the consecrated kalashas, under Srihari’s unique presence.

27.action: Show Āvāhana, Sthāpana, Sannidhāna, Sammukhīkaraṇa, Sannirodhana and Avaguṇṭhana mudrās with the Nārāyaṇa mantra. Offer arghya, pādya, ācamana, madhuparka, second ācamana, bathing water, garments, ornaments, sacred thread and seat with flowers or water in a separate vessel; offer gandha, tulasī and flowers. Worship the kalaśa's āvaraṇa devatās and offer them the listed twelve services, food and salutations along with the pīṭha devatās and principal form. Praise the kalaśa, recite 'Sarva-kṣetra-mayo', then dedicate its worship to Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa with 'Yasya smṛtyā'.
27.contemplate: Contemplate the kalashas as the loci of the devatas and Srihari’s special presence, ready to support every ensuing offering.

28.action: Praise the shankha with the source verses. Draw water with an uddharini from the Snaniya Kalasha; never immerse the shankha to collect water. Keep it only on a pitha. Offer tulasi and flowers; chant “Om Namo Bhagavate Panchajanyaya” and the Gayatri three times; give the eight upacharas, pray to Lakshmi, and make the samarpana.
28.contemplate: The shankha symbolizes Lakshmi. Contemplate Surya and Chandra as its presiding devatas, Varuna in its centre, Prajapati at its back, and Ganga and Saraswati at its tip.

29.action: First worship the Peetha devatas before invoking Bimbaroopa Srihari in the pratimas. Proceed through the source’s full order from the worlds and coverings beneath the Brahmanda up to the peetha, then worship the mantapa, lotus, petals and the devatas stationed on them.
29.contemplate: Visualize the four-legged peetha, its upper and lower portions and phalaka; the cosmic levels below it; and the gold mantapa and lotus arrangement in which each named devata occupies the source-given place. At the heart-lotus level, envision the nine named forms and their Icchā, Jñāna and Kriyā aspects (twenty-seven in all); see gem-adorned Śeṣa as the yoga-seat, with Lakṣmī as the jewel-studded bedding for Paramātmā.

30.action: First offer inward worship to the image of Śrīhari in the heart. Visualize the heart-lotus, turn its downward-facing petals upward with the Vāyu bīja “yaṃ,” then raise and open them with Oṃ as the knowledge of Hari’s supremacy makes the lotus bloom. Meditate on the personal bimba form before invoking it in the outer image.
30.contemplate: Remember the continuous dependence of the jīva on Śrīhari and the bimba–pratibimba relation. See Hari present throughout the body, in the body’s heart-lotus, throughout the energetic jīva and in that jīva’s heart-lotus. The three heart forms are Prādeśa, Mūleśa and Agreśa; the last is the Prājña form invoked outward. Meditate on His radiance, weapons, Śrī, Bhū and attendants as the recording recites.

31.action: Meditate on the named devata forms in their golakas, invoke them in their respective pratimas, and then invoke Srihari as antaryamin within them. Worship first in the heart; lead Him through Sushumna to Brahmarandhra, and request His descent through the left nostril into the pratima, as the linked invocation passages direct.
31.contemplate: See Vayu and Lakshmi as the inner golakas of the pratima and Srihari as their independent indweller. See the heart-form, the invoked pratima-form and the worshipper’s act as connected through the prescribed inward path. In the Viṣṇu, Lakṣmī and Vāyu icons visualize Vāyu as first golaka, Lakṣmī within him as second, and Hari within her; in Garuḍa and Śeṣa icons visualize that deity first, Vāyu second, Lakṣmī third, and Hari within.

32.action: Arrange the six vessels by direction and invoke each presiding deity while showing its mudrā: arghya in the northwest for Śrī with Dhāna mudrā; pādya in the southwest for Sarasvatī with Añjali; ācamana in the northeast for Rati with Gokarṇa; madhuparka in the center for Brahmā with Śūkarī; second ācamana in the center for Śānti with Haṃsa; bathing water in the southeast for Varuṇa with Haṃsa. Put darbha tips, mustard, sesame, fruit, flowers, akṣata, barley and gandha in arghya; Viṣṇuparṇī, sesame, dūrvā, śyāmāka, lotus and akṣata in pādya; clove, nutmeg, berry, cardamom, camphor and gandha in ācamana; curd and honey in madhuparka; the specified fragrant substances in bathing water; clove, nutmeg, berry, gandha and flowers in second ācamana. When ingredients are unavailable, use gandha and tulasī. Sprinkle the consecrated conch water three times over offerings and icons and dedicate the worship to Hari.
32.contemplate: Contemplate each patra as inhabited and governed by the devatas identified in the source table, while Srihari remains their supreme controller. See Hari extend His hands for arghya and see His radiant lotus feet washed with pādya; imagine the scented Gaṅgā water for ācamana and His acceptance of madhuparka.

33.action: Mentally remove Śrīhari's weapons and ornaments, invite Him to the bathing place, and offer golden sandals and royal honors. Perform the Rahasya's pure-water abhiṣeka in its prescribed sequence, including the applicable mantras and separate water collection for the different icons.
33.contemplate: See Srihari initially adorned with His weapons and ornaments, then graciously proceeding to the bathing place; contemplate every bathing offering as worship of the fully divine Bimba. During the Puruṣa Sūkta bath, see the transcendent, thousand-formed Lord present in the image and recognize the fortune of serving Him with your hands.

34.divergence: The recording ends this step with a brief salutation to all āvaraṇa devatās. The Rahasya provides their directional table, a concentric diagram and a separate twelve-service worship; follow those details for the Action.
34.action: Offer gandha, tulasi, flowers and the leaf offerings in the linked source order. Use fresh tender tulasi where available and make the offerings reverently at Srihari’s feet and neck as described. Invoke the āvaraṇa devatās around Śrīhari, with Śrī to His left and Bhū to His right; honor the directional forms in the linked table and diagram with the twelve stated services.
34.contemplate: Tulasi is Srihari’s precious gift and the supreme external puja material. See the garland and flowers as offerings made to the Lord whose presence pervades the act. Visualize the source diagram’s concentric āvaraṇas and the presiding forms facing Hari. Imagine yellow silk, each named ornament, the three Veda devatās in the sacred thread and the Lord accepting sandal and tender tulasī with affection.

35.action: Show dhupa to Narayana together with all Peetha-Avarana devatas, using the ten named dhupa components mixed with cow ghee. Ring the bell. Show the three-wick ghee eka-arati three and a half times from feet to head, then extinguish it as prescribed.
35.contemplate: Contemplate the fragrant dhupa as an offering to Srihari and the surrounding devatas; perceive the lamp as illuminating His complete divine form. See the lamp offered to Hari, whose radiance gives light to the sun and planets.

36.action: Clean the place before Hari, draw a square maṇḍala with the Śrī bīja, and set a three-legged pīṭha or three flowers beneath a plantain leaf or suitable plate. Place a little ghee first, then rice, salt and pickles; serve lickable, drinkable, suckable and chewable foods. Put rice in the center, sweets in the southeast, pāyasa in the northeast, lickable dishes in the southwest, side dishes in the northwest, ghee between rice and pāyasa, and water on the leaf's right. Add tulasī to the separate sprinkling water, repeat the Nārāyaṇa mantra eight times, sprinkle the meal with Viṣṇu Gāyatrī and touch it with the stated mantra. Show Dhenu, Cakra, Garuḍa, Śaṅkha, Meru and Candra mudrās. Invite Hari to the jeweled dining place, offer the five prāṇa oblations and great meal, recite Dvādaśa Stotra with the curtain in place and repeat the mūla mantra 108 times. Give drinking water, after-offering, mouth and hand cleansing, and the remaining stated post-meal services.
36.contemplate: Visualize Srihari with Sri and Bhu on the jeweled dining pedestal, served by devatas. For every food, contemplate the associated abhimani devata and Srihari-form in the complete source table; know the heart-form, pratima-form and naivedya to be one. See the offered foods as nectar-like, served in jewel-studded golden vessels to the self-satisfied Lord who needs nothing.

37.action: After placing the curtain, meditate on Srihari consuming the naivedya, chant Dvadasha Stotra and the moola mantra 108 times, and offer the intervening drinking water as stated. Continue with the source’s after-offerings when the Lord has accepted the food.
37.contemplate: See the ever-satisfied Srihari lovingly accepting the offering for the devotee’s sake; retain the source’s identity of the heart-form, pratima-form and food offering.

38.action: Offer Uttaraposhana as given by Mahalakshmi, entrust the naivedya to Vishvaksena, offer sandals and seat, then provide the prescribed waters for gargling, hands, teeth and feet, including scented hand-cleansing water.
38.contemplate: Visualize Mahalakshmi serving the post-meal nectar with her right hand and Srihari receiving every service in His divine form.

39.divergence: The source details dhupa and three-wick eka-arati; it does not give a separately named “great arati” sequence matching the recording.
39.contemplate: See the lamp as a fragrant ghee offering to Hari. See rows of lamps before Hari, whose brilliance gives light to the sun and planets.

40.divergence: No direct Rahasya passage matching the recording’s Mantra Pushpa sequence was located in the substantive Pooja Rahasya text.

41.divergence: The linked Rahasya offers umbrella, cāmara, mirror and seat while leading Hari to the bathing place. The recording places a separate royal-honors step near the conclusion; its audio order remains unchanged.
41.action: Offer the royal courtesies in the recording’s place: sandals, white umbrella, cāmara, fan, mirror, lights, song, dance and instruments. Use tulasī or water for each service while contemplating Vāyu and other attendants serving Hari.
41.contemplate: Visualize devatas serving Hari amid gem pillars, ruby carpets, festoons, fragrance, Gandharva music and apsara dance.

42.divergence: The source describes shankha abhisheka and warnings about shankha puja, not the recording’s exact shankha-tirtha distribution mantra sequence; it changes neither the timing nor action of that recording step.
42.contemplate: Maintain the source’s distinction between discarded shankha-abhisheka water and the separately handled tirthas.

43.action: Receive Vayu’s second abhisheka tirtha after puja; sprinkle Lakshmi, Sesha and Garuda tirthas on the head rather than drinking them.
43.contemplate: Observe the source’s distinct tirtha destinations.

44.action: Return invoked forms as source directs: merge forms, lead Srihari back to the heart-lotus, perform inner nyasas, ask forgiveness for 32 mistakes, submit the full puja, and say Sri Krishnarpanamastu.
44.contemplate: See bimba Srihari with peetha-avarana devatas re-enter the heart through the sushumna path.

45.action: With bowed head and folded hands repeatedly ask Hari to forgive sins and accept the puja; conclude with the source’s forgiveness and submission sequence.
45.contemplate: Let the prayer arise from sincere repentance and a real desire for liberation, not lip-service.

46.divergence: The Shodashopacāra summary says to perform pradakṣiṇā mentally; the recording and the earlier Rahasya Namaskāra passage also give physical circumambulation and prostration. The guide retains the recording’s physical sequence.
46.action: Walk at least four clockwise pradakṣiṇās very slowly, one foot coming to the other, hands controlled, chanting stotras with the mind on Hari. On the Lord’s right side make at least five namaskāras: lower the left knee, touch the floor with both hands, lower the right knee, touch the forehead, stretch the body like a staff, fold the hands over the head, raise halfway while both knees remain down, then chant and offer praṇāma. Chant the Nārāyaṇa mantra 108 times for completion as the Rahasya directs.
46.contemplate: Keep the mind on Śrīhari during each step and each prostration; see every circumambulation and bowed limb as an offering to Him. The source says these acts remove sins and that His remembrance completes deficiencies in the rite.

47.action: Complete the merging, inner nyasa, forgiveness, dedication and Sri Krishnarpanamastu sequence.
47.contemplate: Contemplate the bimba, its avarana devatas and all invoked forms returned to Hari in the heart.
